When iron comes in contact with $\text{H}^+$ of open air, it donates electrons and turns into $\text{Fe}^{2+}$. It is oxidation.

$$2\text{Fe} \longrightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4\text{e}^-$$

The electrons donated by $\text{Fe}$ is accepted by $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{H}^+$ to produce $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ by reduction.

$$\text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^- \longrightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

At this stage, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{O}_2$ undergo a reaction and produce $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ and water.

$$4\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4\text{H}^+ + \text{O}_2 \longrightarrow 4\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Then, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ undergoes a reaction with $\text{OH}^-$ and produces $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$.

$$\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3\text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{Fe(OH)}_3$$

This ferric hydroxide turns into hydrated ferric oxide or rust $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$2\text{Fe(OH)}_3 \longrightarrow \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

### Experiment of the Formation of Rust

* Take four test tubes and mark them 1 to 4.
* Take the necessary measures to make them similar to the figure.
* Boil the water of test tube 3 for a minute and add $1\text{ mL}$ cooking oil or olive oil to the water. The oil will restrict the air from entering the water.
* Preserve the test tubes in this situation for a week and observe.
